description:
Some existing nodes use models that no longer exist as values on `LlmModel` enum.

### Changes 🏗️

- Update models for all blocks with `LlmModel` fields that do not exist in `LlmModel` enum to `gpt-4o`, directly in `AgentNode->constantInput` db column, on server startup

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
  - [x] Updates wrong models to `gpt-4o` for all affected `AgentNode`s
  - [x] Doesn't update correct models
  - [x] Doesn't insert model when unnecessary
  - [x] Doesn't break other values in jsonb

comments.body:
What if we do that here autogpt_platform/backend/backend/server/rest_api.py
```python
@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan_context(app: fastapi.FastAPI):
    await backend.data.db.connect()
    await backend.data.block.initialize_blocks()
    await backend.data.user.migrate_and_encrypt_user_integrations()
    await backend.data.graph.fix_llm_provider_credentials()
    with launch_darkly_context():
        yield
    await backend.data.db.disconnect()
```

I had to do a raw query because Prisma doesn't handle:
1. Checking if a key exists in jsonb column (and throws when checks value for non-existing key)
2. Updating individual value for a key in jsonb

-> 1. would force me to get all AgentNodes (*a lot* of nodes if we remove popular model in future) and 2. to update entire json for each AgentNode individually.
I think this query is safe, none of the variables come from the user.
